findings.title: Python closures miss every file a spawned child process reads; select() skips the script on a change to it
findings.claim: 31 (script, file) pairs across tests/doc_claims.py and tests/deployment_shape.py, and 883 across entities.py, features.py and harness_headers.py, are files the script's child processes read that the script's committed closure omits, so closure.select([file]) returns mode scoped with the script skipped; a one-line tests/hastub edit turns deployment_shape.py red while select() skips it.
findings.mechanism: tests/closure.py:_exec_record records a Python script in-process under sys.addaudithook plus sys.modules. A child process's reads never reach the hook, and only the child's argv is kept. The node lane records under strace -f, but the Python lanes do not. tests/closure.py check re-records with the same blind instrument, so the table is checked against itself and cannot flag these seams. Instances: doc_claims.py spawns tests/plan_view.py, whose payload make_model_figures.demand_windows draws; 9 hastub files are missing. deployment_shape.py spawns its own '-P --driver' child, which imports the integration against tests/hastub; its closure holds no hastub file, so 22 are missing.

findings.proposed_fix_scope: Barrier in tests/closure.py. On Linux, record a Python script as _record_node_strace records node: wrap --exec-record in strace -f -qq -y -e trace=openat, take the ABSOLUTE path strace -y prints for the returned fd, and union the result with the audit-hook set, which stays for Darwin and for #1309's .pyc attribution. That retires the DRIVEN_BY_OTHERS hand rule's reason. Decide explicitly whether git-internal reads (git grep, git status) count as dependencies; card_drift.mjs's strace already records them. Standing cost falls only on main's closures job, which re-records anyway: 9.4 s strace wall vs 5.9 s recorded audit-hook seconds on the default set (provisional). Partial, cheaper alternative: a _widen rule giving deployment_shape.py all of tests/hastub, and a closure union doc_claims.py <- plan_view.py. That closes today's 31 but not the next child.

findings.title: Mutation ratchet inventory cannot see 528 of 2313 production guard seams; a new guard of those shapes raises it by 0
findings.claim: tests/mutation_table.py:candidates() yields no site on 528 of the 2313 guard seams in custom_components/heatpump_optimizer (52 of 1346 early-exit ifs, 246 of 668 clamps, 230 of 299 threshold ternaries). A new undispositioned guard whose test spans two lines therefore raises unpinned_sites by 0 and ratchet_refusal does not refuse, against +1 and refusal for the same guard on one line.
findings.mechanism: Six single-line operators. GUARD_OFF fires only on an if whose test is on one line, whose line starts with 'if ' and ends with ':', and which has no else; that misses multi-line tests (46), elif (3), a trailing comment after the colon (2) and else branches (1). CLAMP_DROP fires only on a bare min/max with exactly 2 args on one line; that misses numpy/math clamps (179), multi-line calls (63) and 3+ args (4). No operator touches a conditional expression's test. At their pre-fix commits, two of the six ledger I1 instances whose defect is a guard line are of an invisible shape: R5 D3-04 #1312 (the ternary len(positives) >= 2, 076f4a35^) and R5 D3-08 #1316 (np.clip in curve_learning._step_down, 6438f8f6^).

evidence.unit: guard seams with no candidates() site on their line
evidence.machine: box B9 cloud container, 4 cores, Linux 6.18, CPython 3.14.0rc2

perturbation.change: --perturb widen: wrap candidates() so it also yields GUARD_OFF for every ast.If (the fix shape for the EXIT arm), in memory

findings.metric_definition: Count of AST guard seams (EXIT if/elif ending in an exit; CLAMP min/max with >=2 args or np/math clamp; TERN compare/finite ternary) with no candidates() site of the covering kind on that line.
findings.phenomenon_property: Every production guard (early-exit if, clamp, threshold ternary) has a candidate site in mutation_table.inventory(), so unpinned_sites counts it until it carries a disposition, and a new undispositioned guard raises the ratchet.

null_control.note: A clean module with single-line guards and 2-arg clamps gives 0. The one-line re-introduction (the same guard's test split over two lines) gives 1. The ratchet probe drives the production inventory -> unpinned_sites -> ratchet_refusal chain over a scratch copy of price_model.py.

reproduction_steps: guard_inventory.py --history: #1312 TERN invisible, #1313 CLAMP inventoried, #1314 EXIT inventoried, #1315 EXIT inventoried, #1316 CLAMP invisible, #1317 CLAMP inventoried

Context, not a finding: at baseline 3677 of 3951 inventoried sites are unpinned. That includes price_model.py:227 and topology.py:647, whose pins merged in 076f4a35 and 6438f8f6, because the ledger lags the pins by design (growth-only ratchet).
Top files by invisible seams: optimizer.py 152, coordinator.py 135, thermal_model.py 77, sysid.py 27
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Barrier in tests/mutation_table.py:candidates(). GUARD_OFF on any ast.If, rewriting the test's source segment (multi-line and elif included) to False. CLAMP_DROP on np.clip/np.minimum/np.maximum/np.fmin/np.fmax/math.fmin/fmax and on multi-line min/max calls. A seventh TERN operator that replaces a conditional expression's test with True. Mutants become multi-line edits, which per-worker tree copies already allow. Standing cost is AST-only: inventory() takes 3.77 s CPU today and this detector 3.91 s (provisional). The widening adds 528 sites at base and head alike, so no PR is refused by the widening itself, and the nightly burn-in inherits 528 more candidates to drive.
